```shiploop-state
{
  "evidence_refs": [
    "Original request S1–S13 and intake guidance",
    "Host-provided descriptions of until-loop, backchain, ralph-loop and shiploop",
    "README.md",
    "package.json",
    "docs/api.md",
    "docs/operations.md",

    "scripts/weekly-report.js",
    "src/app.js",

    "src/notifier.js",
    "src/templates.js",
    "src/server.js",
    "test/query.test.js",
    "test/api.test.js"
  ],
  "headline": "Intake mapped the ticket-service changes and identified an unresolved weekly reporting window.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "question_categories": [
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K1"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K2"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K3"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K4"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K5"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K6"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K7"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K8"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K9"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K10"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K11"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K12"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K13"}
  ],
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "What are the weekly report window's start, end, time zone and ticket timestamp? Discovery should first check the report, its documentation and any available support-lead or operations sources.",
      "changes": "The closed-ticket filter, its boundary tests and API documentation.",
      "route": "person",
      "default": "If no source or person settles it, assume tickets closed in the preceding seven days through the request time, in UTC, using the close transition time; this is an assumption, not the existing report's verified rule.",
      "blocks": "The final weekly-window contract and its acceptance tests until discovery and the support lead settle it, or the recorded default is adopted."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "How should a recent resolution notice suppress a closure notice, including pending, sent and dead events? Discovery should first inspect the outbox history, delivery timestamps and existing deduplication behavior.",
      "changes": "Notification eligibility and tests for timing, delivery state and reopen cycles.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Suppress a closure notice for the same ticket and requester when a resolution notice is pending or was sent in the preceding 24 hours; a dead notice does not count as delivered. Record the 24-hour threshold as an assumption.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds after discovery checks whether existing evidence establishes a different rule."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "How should immediate delivery and batching coexist for a bulk close? Discovery should first inspect the notifier, relay format and worker scheduling.",
      "changes": "The batch message, recipient grouping, delivery timing and observable acceptance tests.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Group eligible closures by requester within one bulk call, include each ticket in one notice per requester, and make it due on the next worker tick without an additional waiting window; a single close produces a single-ticket notice.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds after discovery checks compatibility with the existing relay and retry contract."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What bulk-close HTTP contract should support 500 tickets? Discovery should first verify whether an existing route, client or documented contract supplies one.",
      "changes": "The endpoint name, request and response shapes, validation, errors and integration tests.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "If no contract exists, add a documented bulk-close endpoint accepting at least 500 ticket IDs and returning results in the existing JSON conventions; validate the complete request before changing tickets and treat an invalid or conflicting member as an atomic failure.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds after discovery establishes existing route and client constraints."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K13",
      "question": "How should repeated close requests reconcile idempotence with a 409 response? Discovery should first confirm the existing transition and audit behavior.",
      "changes": "Repeat-close responses and tests for duplicate changes, audit entries and notifications.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Return 409 for an already-closed ticket while leaving ticket state, audit history and notifications unchanged; idempotence refers to effects rather than identical responses.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds after discovery confirms the existing error envelope."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "What state and privacy guarantees can the current runtime support for deduplication, batching and concurrent requests? Discovery should inspect persistence validation, single-process ownership, outbox records and relay visibility.",
      "changes": "The persisted representation, restart and concurrency tests, and notification contents.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the existing single-process store and optional data file; preserve existing records across upgrades, expose each requester only their own ticket details, and make no new authentication or multi-process coordination claim.",
      "blocks": "A durable batch and deduplication design until discovery establishes the existing persistence and relay constraints."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q7",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "Which existing listing and notification behaviors must be preserved while correcting combined filters? Discovery should inspect the API, pagination, CLI, report and notification tests.",
      "changes": "Regression coverage and the scope of code and documentation changes.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve existing single-filter, cursor, lifecycle, CLI column, audit and retry contracts; combine list filters with AND before pagination.",
      "blocks": "The complete regression test matrix until discovery establishes the affected contracts."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K6",
      "question": "Which runtime settings and existing seams constrain a 500-ticket call and notification delivery? Discovery should inspect configuration, request-body limits, store persistence and the worker.",
      "changes": "Bulk validation, persistence strategy and runtime verification.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use Node.js 22 or later and built-in modules only, preserving the configured body limit, worker-off behavior and existing retry logic.",
      "blocks": "The bulk implementation approach until discovery establishes whether a valid 500-ID request fits the existing limits."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K7",
      "question": "Which existing modules provide independently testable seams for list filtering, ticket changes, audit, notification rendering and delivery? Discovery should inspect the store and service composition.",
      "changes": "Module boundaries and the tests needed to observe behavior without bypassing the store.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Extend the existing query, store, template and worker seams; keep ticket mutations and their audit and outbox effects together.",
      "blocks": "The implementation plan until discovery establishes the relevant seams."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "What evidence proves each outcome at the real boundary? Discovery should inspect the Node test harness and determine how to run a server with an isolated data file and observable notification output.",
      "changes": "The test commands, fixtures and live-server acceptance checks.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Require npm test plus running-server HTTP checks for close, repeat close, combined filters, window boundaries, actor audit, notification suppression and batching, and a 500-ticket bulk call.",
      "blocks": "Exit from the later until loop until tests and running-server checks pass."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "Where can the changed service be delivered and exercised, and what access is available? Discovery should inspect the workspace and runtime environment first.",
      "changes": "The checkout handoff and live-server verification setup.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Deliver the changes in this tickets-service checkout and verify them against an isolated local server; no production deployment target is specified.",
      "blocks": "Running-server verification until an environment that permits starting a server is available; this intake cannot start one."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "What practical bounds can be demonstrated for responsiveness and privacy without inventing numeric targets? Discovery should inspect existing service limits and exercise the requested bulk case later.",
      "changes": "Bulk acceptance checks and notification data exposure.",
      "route": "experiment",
      "default": "Require a 500-ticket bulk call to complete successfully under the normal configuration, without imposing an unrequested latency number; preserve the existing internal-network access model.",
      "blocks": "Performance acceptance until a later permitted running-server exercise completes."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q13",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "Can batching and suppression preserve the outbox retry and relay contract across failures and restarts? Discovery should first inspect event keys, saved-state validation and the notifier's output schema.",
      "changes": "The delivery design and failure, restart and duplicate-notification checks.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve the current retry and relay deduplication behavior; stop and report a concrete blocker if the requested behavior cannot be achieved within that boundary.",
      "blocks": "The notification design until discovery establishes compatibility."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q14",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "What do until-loop, backchain and optional ralph-style operation mean in this host, and what cap is available? Discovery should use the host's installed skill descriptions and any accessible skill instructions.",
      "changes": "The later planning and execution workflow and its stopping condition.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Back-chain before implementation, iterate until the specified evidence is green, and cap any unattended loop at 10 iterations or two hours, whichever comes first; do not start an overnight loop during intake.",
      "blocks": "The later execution workflow until discovery checks the available skill instructions."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "S1 [fact]: The target is the help-desk ticket service in this folder, with HTTP consumers, requester notifications and operator tooling.\\nS2 [outcome; assumption Q2]: A closure should notify its requester while suppressing a sufficiently recent resolution notice.\\nS3 [outcome; assumption Q3]: Make eligible notices due promptly and group closures for the same requester within a bulk call.\\nS4 [outcome; open Q1]: The list endpoint needs a closed-ticket time window; the checked weekly report counts all listed tickets and establishes no such window.\\nS5 [fact and outcome]: Documented list filters must intersect before pagination.\\nS6 [fact]: The current matcher uses OR for multiple filters, so the assumption that they already combine correctly is contradicted by the code.\\nS7 [boundary and outcome]: Back-chain before implementation, then iterate until tests and checks against a running server pass.\\nS8 [boundary; assumption Q14]: Overnight operation is optional and any unattended loop needs a finite cap.\\nS9 [outcome]: Verify observable behavior with substantive tests and keep documentation accurate and economical.\\nS10 [boundary]: Preserve outbox retry logic; migration away from OldTracker is context, not requested implementation.\\nS11 [boundary]: Use the existing zero-dependency Node.js approach.\\nS12 [outcome; assumption Q5]: A repeated close returns 409 without repeating effects, and the original close records the actor.\\nS13 [outcome]: A single bulk call must successfully close 500 eligible tickets; no numeric latency target was requested.\\nInteraction and state [facts]: Agents call the HTTP API; X-Actor supplies an unverified actor name or defaults to system, and the ticket requester identifies the notification recipient. The store owns tickets, audit and outbox state in one process; DATA_FILE makes it survive restart, otherwise it lasts only for the process. The notifier uses a relay file or memory, and the worker can be disabled. [Assumption Q6]: No new identity system, cross-process coordination or broader visibility is implied; notices should reveal only the recipient's own ticket details.\\nDiscovery leads [hints, not verified facts]: Repository API and operations docs, weekly-report script, support leads, operations owners, mail-relay contract and any available team workspace or internal documentation; no channel, private repository or internal site was named. 'Weekly window', 'just got one', 'right away' and bulk-call semantics remain the specific ambiguous terms. Host skill descriptions establish the best available meanings of until-loop, backchain and optional ralph-loop; detailed installed instructions remain a discovery lead.\\nAuthority and visibility [facts]: This exercise permits read-only inspection in the working directory, no changes and no server during intake. The requested eventual target is this service checkout; in an isolated run the source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, and a deployed outcome would exist only after release. No deployment target or release authority was specified. No prior run was identified."
}
```

commands.command: /bin/zsh -lc "rg -n -i 'week|window|bulk|batch|clos|recent|dedup|oldtracker|filter' README.md docs scripts src test CONTRIBUTING.md CHANGELOG.md"
